subsystems.label: Python Core
subsystems.blurb: Domain model, rule engine and the durable delivery pipeline. Owns the Telegram sessions and the database.

subsystems.label: Go API
subsystems.blurb: Stateless REST control plane. Authenticates clients, applies tenant scoping, and speaks gRPC to the core and the logger.

subsystems.label: Web gateway
subsystems.blurb: Serves the compiled dashboard, proxies the REST API and streams the live log feed over SSE.

subsystems.label: Dashboard UI
subsystems.blurb: Task control, log explorer, diagnostics and admin surfaces for a signed-in tenant.

subsystems.label: Mobile app
subsystems.blurb: Native client with its own 10-locale catalog and the same REST contract as the dashboard.

subsystems.label: DevOps CLI
subsystems.blurb: Install, validate, diagnose and upgrade the stack from one command surface.

subsystems.label: Interfaces
subsystems.blurb: The gRPC service definitions, the generated Go stubs and the cross-language JSON fixtures that pin the wire format.

subsystems.label: This website
subsystems.blurb: The site you are reading, generated from the same checkout it documents.

contracts.label: Control plane → engine
contracts.detail: Every rule, session and delivery command crosses this boundary as a protobuf RPC.

contracts.label: Control plane → log store
contracts.detail: The API writes its own logs, audits and latency events to the same central store.

contracts.label: Engine → log store
contracts.detail: Pipeline stages emit [PIPELINE:*] events through the shared log client.

contracts.label: Engine → AI provider
contracts.detail: Optional rewrite pass. Unreachable provider degrades to pass-through, never to data loss.

contracts.label: Gateway → REST API
contracts.detail: Server-side proxy keeps the API key out of the browser and streams the live log feed.

contracts.label: Dashboard → gateway
contracts.detail: The React app only ever talks to its own origin; the gateway owns upstream addressing.

contracts.label: Mobile app → REST API
contracts.detail: Same REST contract as the dashboard, with offline-tolerant error surfaces.

contracts.label: CLI → running stack
contracts.detail: Diagnostics read the same endpoints an operator would curl.

contracts.label: TLS profile → gateway
contracts.detail: Optional --profile tls terminates TLS and forwards to the gateway.

contracts.label: proto → generated stubs
contracts.detail: The Go stubs and the Python servicers are both generated from one .proto file.

contracts.label: proto → engine servicers
contracts.detail: One schema, two runtimes; a mismatch fails at the gRPC boundary, not in production.

contracts.label: Website → checkout
contracts.detail: The site derives its numbers from the same files a contributor edits.

verifiedAbsences.label: Mobile speaks no gRPC
verifiedAbsences.claim: The mobile client never dials the engine directly: every call goes through the REST control plane.

verifiedAbsences.label: No secrets in the browser bundle
verifiedAbsences.claim: Neither the API key, the master key nor the AI provider address is shipped to the browser.

verifiedAbsences.label: No label chosen by a language branch
verifiedAbsences.claim: A localised label is never picked by a hardcoded ternary — the catalogue lookup does it, and it falls back to English. (The language switcher itself still shows the target language natively, which is the point of a switcher.)

verifiedAbsences.label: Two separate databases
verifiedAbsences.claim: The logger never opens the engine database — the log store is its own file.

verifiedAbsences.label: The engine opens no HTTP port
verifiedAbsences.claim: The engine is reachable only over gRPC; there is no HTTP server inside the core.

openChecks.label: No committed credential defaults
openChecks.claim: Every credential in the compose file is an interpolation; no working secret is committed as a default.

flows.title: A post is forwarded
flows.summary: From an incoming Telegram update to a delivered copy in every target chat, with the durable queue absorbing rate limits.

steps.detail: MTProto push from the source chat the session is authorised for.
Album items are aggregated and the update is turned into a domain event.
Matching tasks, per-source/policy overrides, whitelists and blacklists.
Filters, cleaner, shortcodes, replacements — and the optional AI pass.
Only when the task enables it; an unreachable provider passes the text through.
One durable job per target with an ordering key, so bursts keep their order.
Lease-based workers with exponential backoff and FloodWait-aware rescheduling.
Copy mode or native forward, into the target chat or forum topic.
Every stage, drop and outcome lands in the log store with a correlation id.

flows.title: An operator edits a task
flows.summary: A dashboard write travels through the gateway, the REST control plane and gRPC into the engine — with optimistic concurrency and an audit trail.

steps.detail: A tenant-scoped token is attached to the request; no API key ever reaches the browser.
The Rust gateway forwards to the API and keeps upstream addressing server-side.
Correlation id, access log, log-policy gate and audit event are applied first.
Fail-closed tenant check: the rule is only touched if it belongs to the caller.
The write becomes a protobuf call on the engine surface.
Optimistic concurrency on the rule version; metadata[content_policy] carries the per-task rules.
Transactional write plus the outbox entry used for audit.
Before/after images are written to the log store for attribution.

flows.title: An event is investigated
flows.summary: Live logs, the diagnostic window and the dead-letter queue: how an operator answers "what happened to that message?".

steps.detail: Filters by task, stage, severity and correlation id.
SSE feed so the view updates without polling.
Bounded window, tenant-scoped, with redaction already applied upstream.
Field-aware redaction happens at write time, so even an admin read is already safe.
Bounded-label stats and slow-query events are exposed alongside the rows.
Inspect, replay or purge failed deliveries for the tenant.
